text:
Alex K: filing a quick observation from canary: a few prefixes end up with brief stale reads after ownership transfer. i instrumented an "epoch-ack" window that shows reads served while owner_map already points to new epoch but cache entries still have old epoch. logs:
```
2026-03-25T15:40:01Z HANDOFF start prefix=acct/999 from=shard-11 to=shard-2 epoch=311
2026-03-25T15:40:01Z OWNERSHIP announce prefix=acct/999 epoch=311
2026-03-25T15:40:01Z READ served_from_cache=true cached_epoch=310 owner_epoch=311
```
this produces ~120ms stale window occasionally. thought: call this the "late-binding" problem where routing binds to owner early before cache binds to the new snapshot.
text_followups: Maria D: late-binding is a good name. curious if the old cached blob is missing an apply marker or if the owner_map update races ahead of prefill completion.

Samir R: two orthogonal counters: (1) strict: don't advertise owner until local snapshot apply ACK (atomic bind). (2) pragmatic: keep advertise fast but add a small epoch-ack grace on read-side: if owner_epoch > cached_epoch but (now - owner_announce_ts) < ack_window_ms, reject serve and do sync-check-once. ack_window could be 200ms.

Lee P: i like the pragmatic path for low-risk. details: read path should consult owner_map and owner_announce_ts. If owner_age < ack_window and cached_epoch < owner_epoch -> do synchronous store read and backfill cache. Otherwise, serve stale if customer tolerant? we should be conservative and prefer fresh for hot prefixes.

Nora T: ops concerns: the sync store read will add tail latency; if ack_window too long we'll cause lots of sync backfills. we need heuristics: only perform sync-check for prefixes with recent writes (last_write_ts within X ms) or for prefixes in hot-tier. else allow eventual fixup.

Alex K: suggestion: ack_window=150ms default; perform sync-check if last_write_ts >= owner_announce_ts - 500ms or prefix in hotset. also publish eviction-hint on the invalidation channel so other nodes can proactively drop entries when ack succeeds.

Samir R: implementation notes: owner_map will hold {epoch, announce_ts}. read path check is a single atomic load (RCU snapshot) and compare ints. Add metric evict.epoch_ack_triggered and histogram of added latency so we can tune ack_window.

Lee P: invalidation messages should be idempotent and small: {prefix, new_epoch, announce_ts, ack=true|false}. subscribers do: if ack==true drop cached entries, if ack==false optionally prefetch. include nonce for traceability.

Maria D: product tradeoff: for hosted customers we might default to more conservative (sync-check) to protect linearizable-looking behavior; for certain enterprise customers we can expose a "handoff-atomic" toggle that disables advertise-until-ack and forces atomic bind—higher latency but stronger semantics.

Nora T: add a defensive cooldown: if more than N epoch_ack sync-checks per-second happen for a node, flip to lazy mode for that prefix for 1s to avoid thundering herd. ops will add alert when evict.epoch_ack_triggered rate > threshold.

Samir R: i'll PR read-path epoch-ack check under a feature flag and add unit tests: simulate lost invalidation, delayed prefill, and race between announce and read. also version cache entry blob with a 1-byte schema header so we can change backends safely.

Lee P: infra: i'll add the ack field to the invalidation topic and wire the post-apply ACK path to publish ack=true. also add a per-prefix backoff table so we can suppress repeated invalidations on cold prefixes.

Alex K: operational runbook: when ack-trigger metric spikes, ops should look at prefill latency histogram and invalidation channel delivery failures. default rollback is disable epoch-ack feature flag and revert publisher. make a dashboard with these panels.
Maria D: also add customer-facing query to find tenants who saw reads that didn't match their write timestamp in last 24h. CS should be able to contact them proactively if large.

Samir R: small concern: reading owner_announce_ts requires clock alignment across nodes. we'll keep timestamps from a single monotonic source per control-plane and propagate announce_ts as logical counter if needed to avoid clock skew.
Lee P: good call. use monotonic counters per-shard (handoff sequence id) instead of wall-clock for owner_announce. easier to reason about in read path comparisons.
Nora T: ops will add alerting for invalidation-delivery-failure and a kill-switch env var to immediately disable publisher if rehydrate QPS > baseline*2.
evict-bot: NOTICE: ack-window experiment enabled on canary pool. metrics evict.epoch_ack_triggered will be emitted.

Alex K: plan: Samir -> PR for epoch-ack read guard + tests, Lee -> invalidation ack wiring + nonce + backoff, Nora -> dashboards + kill-switch, Maria -> customer-impact query, Alex -> draft RFC for atomic bind option. aim to land behind flag and run canary 72h, then tune ack_window.
Maria D: ack. will put the rollout plan in the sprint board and schedule a quick sync after canary.
Samir R: starting on the PR. will add microbench numbers to ensure read-path overhead < 1% on p95.
Lee P: infra pieces in queue; will post merge when done.
Alex K: thanks folks. this should let us mitigate customer-visible stale reads without a heavy control-plane refactor immediately. closing once canary passes.
